title: Pressure-Dependent hcp-to-fcc Phase Transition Path Derived from Exact Lattice Summations over Inverse Power Law Potentials
authors: Tage W. Maltby, Andres Robles-Navarro, Jonathan K. Hartlaub, Andreas A. Buchheit, Øivind Wilhelmsen, Morten Hammer, Peter Schwerdtfeger
abstract: We investigate the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) structures along the Burgers-Bain transformation path at pressures up to several hundred gigapascals. We consider a hierarchy of interatomic potentials, from $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials to extended Lennard-Jones two-body interactions in terms of inverse-power expansions and the Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term, alongside density functional theory (DFT) calculations for solid argon. For inverse-power potentials, free energies are evaluated through exact lattice sums and efficient integral representations based on generalizations of the Epstein zeta function to anisotropic interaction kernels, followed by lattice-parameter optimization. This methodology enables an accurate determination of the pressure-dependent Burgers-Bain minimum-energy path and the associated activation barrier for the phase transition. The transformation exhibits pronounced symmetry breaking connecting the Burgers and Bain paths, a feature confirmed by DFT calculations. At high pressure, the hcp-to-fcc activation barrier increases approximately linearly with pressure, owing to the dominant pressure-volume contribution. Including entropy and anharmonic effects yields excellent agreement with experimental temperature-dependent volumes up to the melting point. DFT results also highlight the increasing importance of many-body interactions under compression. Whereas two-body potentials predict that the path passes through the body-centered cubic (bcc) structure only at very high pressures, DFT generally predicts a pathway that bypasses bcc. The Axilrod-Teller-Muto term slightly reduces this discrepancy. Furthermore, DFT performs better at high pressures, where dispersion forces become less important.
summary: This work calculates the structural phase transition path between hcp and fcc crystal phases under extreme pressure using advanced lattice summation techniques. By combining generalized Lennard-Jones potentials with DFT, the authors accurately map the minimum-energy path and predict how the transition barrier evolves with pressure. The results confirm key structural features, such as symmetry breaking, and provide an accurate equation of state up to the melting point.
main_problem: The paper investigates the pressure-dependent minimum-energy path and associated activation barrier for the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structures.
main_result: The transition pathway exhibits a pronounced symmetry-breaking feature, and the activation barrier increases approximately linearly with pressure at high compression.
method: Free energies are evaluated using exact lattice summations based on generalizations of the Epstein zeta function for inverse-power potentials, supplemented by Density Functional Theory (DFT) comparisons.
model_or_system: The system models close-packed crystal structures (hcp, fcc, bcc) undergoing a phase transition along the Burgers-Bain path, using interatomic potentials like (n,m)-Lennard-Jones and the Axilrod-Teller-Muto term.
key_observables: Pressure-dependent minimum-energy path, activation barrier, equation of state (V(T)), and lattice parameters ($\gamma_1, \gamma_2$).
important_parameters: Pressure ($P$) up to several hundred gigapascals, and the phase-transition parameter $\alpha \in [0, 1]$.
main_assumptions: The methodology relies on exact lattice sums for inverse-power potentials and includes anharmonic effects for temperature dependence, though the zero-temperature limit is noted in some contexts.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the primitive monoclinic cell in the Burgers transformation, showing basis vectors for hcp, fcc, and bcc. Table I provides ideal lattice parameters for the three structures.
paper_structure: The work systematically derives the cohesive and free energies along the parameterized Burgers-Bain path, optimizing lattice parameters using Newton-Raphson procedures, and comparing results across various potential models and DFT calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical solid-state physics, the rigorous mathematical treatment of lattice sums using advanced functions like the Epstein zeta function demonstrates sophisticated techniques applicable to calculating many-body interactions in complex quantum systems.
